It is LEVEL: the house's verticals stand vertical in the print, so the principal point is set on the horizon, which the front's cornice and base lines put at about y 1250 px. FIT: a least-squares fit of eye, heading, focal length and horizon to six readings: the south-west corner at the sheet's corner feature (u 25.5, v 16.9) at grade and at the cornice's top (x 848, y 1582 and 832 px), the pavilion's south corner at grade and at the cornice (x 600, y 1565 and 845), the porch's balcony rail at its south end (x 275, y 1126, 7.3 m) and the south flank's far end at the cornice (x 1380, y 982); with the cornice at the record's 12.6 m it puts the eye at u 58.5, v 38.2 (across the avenue, about 22 m south of the corner), 5.2 m over the house's grade (the photographer looks down on the fence's curb and the lawn: an upper window or a stoop across the street), heading 234 degrees, f 2376 px. UNCERTAINTY: the corner feature the fit stands on is the sheet's extent of it, not built yet (T-3172), and the distance trades against every height and width at once; nothing outside the house fixes it, so it is held by the cornice's height and the plan's widths. LIGHT: the front and the corner's south face lit alike by a high sun in the south-west, the street tree's shadow falling across the fence (sun_uvy).
